research_questions: How does sampling temperature change musical diversity, rhythmic consistency, density and repetition?
Do later checkpoints improve generation quality as well as next-token prediction?
How does available context affect continuation structure at a controlled training budget?
Can melody-conditioned generation preserve the complete supplied melody and produce useful accompaniment?

data.source: Official course POP909/training only; three basic prompts and ten bonus prompts are excluded from training.
data.diagnostic_split: Song-level split before window sampling: 851 optimization songs, 45 validation songs; seed 20261022. The 13 official prompt folders are excluded.
data.final_fit: Final checkpoint has observed all 896 official songs, confirmed by training and seen-song ID sets. Its validation loss is unset; earlier validation estimates describe only pre-refit diagnostic models.
data.beat_grid: Supplied beat/downbeat annotations define bars; MIDI time-signature metadata is not treated as authoritative.
data.basic_tracks: Merge all MELODY, BRIDGE and PIANO source note events; role training retains MELODY and PIANO separately.

tokenizer.representation: Beat-annotation-aware REMI: BOS, Bar, Meter, Tempo, then Pos/Pitch/Velocity/Duration note tuples; EOS. Bonus retains Track_Melody and Track_Piano roles.
tokenizer.time_grid: Eight subdivisions per supplied annotation beat; up to sixteen beats per bar; duration 1..256 steps (32 beats).
tokenizer.velocity: 32 bins; exact original prompt velocities are retained in final exports.
tokenizer.export_meter: Canonical annotation-beat notation: one supplied annotation beat is written as one quarter note and Meter_n as n/4. This preserves bar counts and elapsed time; the beat annotations do not identify the original score denominator (six pulses are exported as6/4, not claimed to recover6/8).
tokenizer.pickup_policy: Retain an annotated short pickup bar; clamp notes before the first annotation timestamp to the first grid position and disclose the measured error.
tokenizer.quantization_ablation: Actual 4/8/16-resolution reconstruction audit below; models are trained only at resolution eight.
tokenizer.decoding_constraints: Grammar masks legal next-token types, ascending pitch order for simultaneous notes, complete bar boundaries, pitch21..108, end-time-safe durations and a 64-note-per-bar cap; these are disclosed inference rules.

model.attention: Decoder-only causal self-attention; learned absolute positions, pre-layer normalization, GELU feed-forward layers, tied token embedding/output weights.
model.context_rollover: On overflow, retain the latest complete bars fitting the context, prepend BOS and rebuild the key/value cache. Position indices restart; this limits long-range memory.

training.optimizer: AdamW; betas(0.9,0.95), weight decay0.1, norm clipping1.0; warmup and cosine decay. Per-stage values and measured target-token counts are saved in the source histories.
training.augmentation: Training-window transposition sampled uniformly from legal integer shifts -5..+5 semitones, preserving piano-range pitch21..108; validation uses no augmentation.
training.window_sampling: Shuffle songs, visit each selected song before repeating, and sample a bar-aligned window. Labels use nonpadding targets only; no target crosses a song boundary.
training.curve_scope: Shown curve concatenates basic_diagnostic and basic_refined optimizer steps. Validation uses a deterministic song-level pre-refit split. All-song stages have no held-out validation loss.
training.no_human_listening_claim: No human listener ratings or listening comparisons were collected; selection uses explicitly described objective diagnostics.

basic_a.baseline_protocol: One deterministic center-nearest eligible 32-bar crop from each of 45 pre-refit validation songs; nearest eligible crop for rare meters. Shared Pos8-to-Pos16 adapter and official128-position dictionary; 2000 whole-piece bootstrap draws with seed8173. These songs participate in the final all896-song fit, so this reference is descriptive and is not independent of that final model.

bonus.method: The roles Transformer reads only the supplied melody and annotation beat grid, forces MELODY tokens as context at each bar, and samples PIANO notes. Export restores the original melody notes; ground-truth piano/chords are used only by the evaluator.

aggregate.interpretation: CA is a coarse triad-estimator agreement; CA-ceiling means the same estimator applied to ground truth, not a strict mathematical upper bound. OA uses distributions and can overlook octave displacement and temporal ordering.

additional_experiments.name: Equal-token context-length comparison
additional_experiments.method: Two branches start from the same refined checkpoint SHA256. Both use AdamW, learning rate 0.00008 and a 4,000,000 non-padding target budget. Compare last checkpoints on the same 45-song, 2048-token validation windows; allow at most one training-step budget overshoot.
additional_experiments.analysis: The 2048-token branch has lower validation CE (1.70637 versus 1.74084) and is selected before the all-song final fit. The measured token-budget difference is 3,454 targets (0.086% of the nominal budget).
additional_experiments.limitations: One run per context, with different batch sizes and step counts. The shared parent was trained mainly at 2048 tokens with learned absolute positions; the 4096 branch must adapt later positions. Validation also uses 2048 tokens. This compares this warm start and budget, not the general value of long context.

additional_experiments.name: What improves when token loss falls?
additional_experiments.method: Teacher-forced full-vocabulary prediction with no grammar mask: 77,926 non-padding targets from the same 48 deterministic windows covering all 45 pre-refit validation songs. Window hashes match across the step-500 and step-2000 checkpoints.
additional_experiments.analysis: Overall CE falls from 2.36666 to 1.97120 nats/token and top-1 accuracy rises from 26.54% to 35.51%. Token-family accuracy is already 98.30% at step 500; pitch-content accuracy rises from 8.71% to 19.30% and remains much harder than recognizing token grammar.
additional_experiments.limitations: Teacher forcing supplies the correct history and does not measure free-running musical quality. These checkpoints were trained on the 851-song optimization split; the final all-song models are not claimed to have held-out validation accuracy.

additional_experiments.name: Quantization resolution: reconstruction cost
additional_experiments.method: All 896 original training songs; identical annotation beat maps, rounding, velocity bins, merged tracks, 32-beat maximum duration. Position vocabulary supports 16 beats per bar at every resolution. No Transformer is retrained for this ablation.
additional_experiments.analysis: Across 1,508,536 notes, finer grids reduce mean timing error and same-pitch collisions while increasing vocabulary size. Eight steps/beat is the implemented compromise. This reconstruction study does not compare retrained model quality. The same two duration-cap outliers and early-note clamp errors persist.

additional_experiments.name: Codec round-trip verification
additional_experiments.method: MIDI source to quantized tokens, decode using original annotation clock, independent pretty_midi readback; checks count, pitch, quantized velocity and all note times. Includes compound/three-beat meter, largest pickup error and both duration-cap songs.
additional_experiments.analysis: All cases pass independent readback within2ms of quantized timing. This does not imply lossless source reconstruction: two notes exceed the32beat duration cap (max offset error8.732s); pre-annotation notes are clamped (max onset error0.709s). These are disclosed representation limits.

additional_experiments.name: Sampling temperature and truncation
additional_experiments.method: Frozen final checkpoint,20 independent32bar samples per setting, identical seed schedule and canonical official metric adapter. Whole-piece bootstrap confidence intervals are stored with the primary metrics.
additional_experiments.analysis: The stated metric-distance rule selects t12, with standardized mean gap=0.6155. All settings retain their complete20piece output sets.
additional_experiments.discussion: Entropy describes pitch-class diversity; GS describes onset-pattern consistency. Density, rest and repetition diagnostics are needed to interpret them. Paired5000draw whole-piece bootstrap differences versus t10 are saved in paired_sampling_comparisons.json.
additional_experiments.limitations: The same reported sets are used for configuration selection. The real-data reference is not independent of the all896song final refit. No human listening study was performed.

additional_experiments.name: Checkpoint learning diagnostics
additional_experiments.method: Diagnostic checkpoints are evaluated on independently generated20piece32bar sets using the same seed schedule and canonical adapter.
additional_experiments.analysis: Only completed20piece sets are included; partial generation manifests are excluded from this comparison.
additional_experiments.discussion: The500step model already has GS close to the real reference while generating roughly half its note density. Similar GS therefore does not establish realistic arrangement or musical quality.
additional_experiments.limitations: These are pre-refit diagnostic checkpoints, not the all896song final model. Different effective contexts can also influence generation, so checkpoint changes are not an isolated causal experiment.

additional_experiments.name: Official GS normalization sensitivity
additional_experiments.method: Keep the unchanged official128position GS and also report a separately named diagnostic using max(meter_a,meter_b)*8 active positions per bar pair.
additional_experiments.analysis: The canonical adapter maps the model8subdivisions/beat to16 by multiplying positions by2. Odd positions and positions outside the active meter remain zero; this raises official GS relative to the active-grid diagnostic.
additional_experiments.discussion: Both scores are shown without substituting the diagnostic for the required official metric. Real and generated sets use exactly the same adapter.
additional_experiments.limitations: GS ignores pitch, duration, note velocity and note multiplicity at one onset. It cannot certify melody, harmony or expressive phrasing.

additional_experiments.name: Exact local training matches
additional_experiments.method: Hash contiguous bars as position8/pitch/duration8 multisets, ignoring tempo, velocity and track names; compare every generated window to every bar of all896 final-refit training songs.
additional_experiments.analysis: Nonempty-window match fractions exclude fully silent windows. Raw silent-window matches remain available in each copy_per_piece.csv, avoiding an interpretation of shared silence as copied musical phrases.
additional_experiments.discussion: Every generated piece is retained in this check, with no metric-based removal.
additional_experiments.limitations: Zero exact matches does not establish originality: transposed, approximate, shifted, velocity-only or partial-note copying can escape this test.

additional_experiments.name: Continuation boundary continuity
additional_experiments.method: Compare two bars immediately before and after the8bar prompt boundary. Within each prompt minimize |log density ratio|+|pitch mean jump|/12+(1-pitch-class Jaccard).
additional_experiments.analysis: Best settings under this fixed symbolic rule are 001:t12, 002:t12, 003:t10. Original8bar note pitch, velocity and timing identity are separately checked from the MIDI files.
additional_experiments.discussion: A low boundary score indicates a smaller local change in note density and pitch content; abrupt changes can still be musically valid.
additional_experiments.limitations: Two-bar statistics do not assess phrase completion, later24bar development or listener preference. Supplemental full32bar H4/GS includes the supplied prefix; continuation-only24bar metrics are saved separately.

additional_experiments.name: Bonus melody-conditioning ablation
additional_experiments.method: Same roles checkpoint,10 identical prompts and seed schedule,T1/top-p.95. Remove MELODY note quartets while keeping bar/meter/tempo/track headers; restore the complete original melody in both exports. Evaluate the unchanged official CA/OA and bootstrap paired whole prompts5000times.
additional_experiments.analysis: Across these ten paired prompts, normal-minus-empty intervals lie above zero for CA, OA_V, OA_D, below zero for no metrics, and include zero for OA_P, OA_IOI. The five percentile intervals are unadjusted; they describe this intervention and do not establish a causal improvement in musical quality.
additional_experiments.discussion: Positive normal-minus-empty differences favor the normal condition on that metric; negative differences favor the empty condition. Confidence intervals and all10 paired prompt rows are retained.
additional_experiments.limitations: Removing all MELODY notes is an out-of-distribution intervention and changes context length and later sampled histories. It cannot isolate a causal effect on musical quality. Both outputs restore exactly the original melody; the empty variant is evaluation-only and is excluded from the formal submission.

additional_experiments.name: Bonus sampling temperature selection
additional_experiments.method: Hold the roles checkpoint, ten melody prompts, seed schedule and top-p .95 fixed; compare normal-conditioning temperatures .8, 1.0 and 1.2. Select the largest equal-weight average of the five official CA/OA metrics.
additional_experiments.analysis: The predefined composite selects t10 (T=1.0), mean=0.5771. Its difference from runner-up t12 is +0.0045, paired 95% interval [-0.0216, +0.0295]. The fixed T1 baseline is retained for the conditioning ablation.
additional_experiments.discussion: All ten prompts remain in each condition. Paired prompt-bootstrap differences from T1 and all per-prompt composite values are saved with the evidence.
additional_experiments.limitations: Temperature selection uses the same10 provided prompts and evaluation ground truth; this is in-sample tuning without an independent test. A larger composite or individual metric does not establish better music or listener preference. The fixed T1 conditioning-ablation baseline is preserved separately.

additional_experiments.name: Real-data reference sensitivity
additional_experiments.method: Same deterministic center-nearest eligible32bar crop per song and identical canonical16subdivision/128position adapter. All896 official songs were considered; short or unrepresentable songs are listed individually.
additional_experiments.analysis: Primary45 minus all-reference mean shifts are H4=-0.008 full-set standard deviations, GS=+0.015 full-set standard deviations, notes_per_bar=+0.082 full-set standard deviations. The all-reference mean falls inside the primary45 whole-piece bootstrap interval for 3/3 descriptors. The subset closely matches the full eligible set under these measured descriptors; this supports its descriptive use here, without establishing representative musical style or perceived quality.
additional_experiments.discussion: Selected t12 minus primary45: H4=+0.1448, GS=-0.0007, notes_per_bar=-1.9075. Selected t12 minus all_eligible: H4=+0.1439, GS=-0.0004, notes_per_bar=-1.4449. The primary45 reference and selected configuration are retained exactly as specified.
additional_experiments.limitations: The45song set is contained in the full set; these comparisons are descriptive and are not independent hypothesis tests. Agreement on H4/GS/density does not establish representative musical style or perceived quality.

limitations: No human listening or preference ratings were collected; selections use the stated symbolic proxies.

The primary 45-song reference was held out only before the final fit. Both the 45-song and 891-song real references overlap the final model trained on all 896 songs; the final model has no independent test set.
Sampling settings are selected using the displayed generated sets. Bootstrap intervals describe variability over pieces or prompts for one checkpoint, without repeated training seeds.
Generation uses grammar masks, a 64-note cap per bar, fixed generated meter/tempo and context rollover. These choices constrain expression and long-range memory.
Eight positions per beat, quantized velocity and a 32-beat duration cap lose source detail. Original continuation prefixes and bonus melodies are restored after generation and verified separately.
H4 measures pitch-class diversity and GS measures onset consistency with padded position normalization. Neither certifies musical quality; OA histograms also omit note order and pitch register.
The bonus model conditions on melody and beat timing, without explicit chord input. Its measured chord agreement remains low relative to the ground-truth piano self-reference.
Zero exact training-window matches does not rule out approximate, transposed or partial-note copying.
The official metrics are descriptive proxies; no numeric formula converts these values into a course grade.

Removing all MELODY notes is an out-of-distribution intervention and changes context length and later sampled histories. It cannot isolate a causal effect on musical quality. Both outputs restore exactly the original melody; the empty variant is evaluation-only and is excluded from the formal submission.

Temperature selection uses the same10 provided prompts and evaluation ground truth; this is in-sample tuning without an independent test. A larger composite or individual metric does not establish better music or listener preference. The fixed T1 conditioning-ablation baseline is preserved separately.

structured_failure_analysis.scope: Symbolic and signal measurements of unchanged submitted files; no human or model listening claim.

definitions.bar_numbering: 1-based from the first submitted bar; B bars 1-8 are the original prompt, 9-32 are generated.
definitions.primary_stats: Original manifest tokens, identical to music_quality_review: onsets count once each; MIDI pitch; velocity = 4*Vel_token+2; unweighted note-onset PC histogram; NumPy linear-interpolated 95th percentile.
definitions.rhythm: SET of Pos8 onset positions per annotated-beat bar, ignoring pitch/duration/velocity/multiplicity; matching sets do not mean identical music.
definitions.wav_time: Time since start of submitted WAV; waveform starts at MIDI time 0. MIDI musical endpoint excludes the approximately 2-second sound-release tail.
definitions.exact_midi: All actual MIDI pitch multisets and note totals are asserted equal to tokens. Per-bar MIDI onsets use 1 ms boundary tolerance for export rounding; original prompt velocity may differ from the quantized token reconstruction.
definitions.register: MIDI 96 = C7; a descriptive register marker, not a universal quality limit. Pitch comparisons do not establish perceived quality.
definitions.chord: Original, unmodified HW2_scripts/eval_bonus.py: 24 major/minor triads, duration*velocity weighted chroma with BASS_WEIGHT, cosine similarity; reference is maximum-overlap-duration annotation label per bar. Chord annotations are read for post-generation evaluation only.
definitions.reference: The 45 center-nearest 32-bar source crops were included in final all896-song fitting. Register comparisons are descriptive, not held-out generalization.

register_summary.sample_selection: Extreme: greatest whole-piece p95 pitch, ties lexical sample ID. Typical: nearest whole-piece p95 pitch to the 20-piece median, ties lexical ID. Selection diagnoses register only, not overall quality.

report_discussion.register: The t12 setting minimizes the preregistered combined mean H4/GS reference gap among the tested settings, yet its register remains broader and higher than the 45-song reference: mean piece-level pitch p95 is 92.39 versus 78.36, a 14.02-semitone gap. The mean per-piece share of onsets at MIDI 96 or above is 3.50% versus 0.033%. H4 collapses octave information into pitch classes and GS only uses onset positions, so neither proxy can expose this register mismatch. The extreme and median-p95 examples are selected by stated rules rather than listening preference; no pitch clipping or other postprocessing has been applied.
report_discussion.harmony: Bonus 004 matches none of the 16 annotated bar chords; 009 matches 4/16. The exact same 24-triad estimator on GT piano is shown alongside each example, so agreement failures are not automatically equated with perceptual dissonance. The relatively high pitch-class OA reflects distribution overlap, not correct note or chord alignment. Better conditioning should be tested on training-only validation tunes using chord-aware or phrase-aware objectives before sampling settings are selected.
report_discussion.continuation: All nine continuations are compared across the original 8-bar prompt and three generated 8-bar windows. This extends the local two-bar seam criterion to density, pitch, dynamics, and onset-set repetition across the full 24-bar continuation. For prompt 003 at t12, density falls from 33.875 to 9.250 notes/bar and mean pitch rises from 69.08 to 85.27 between the first and last generated windows. The original selected setting for this prompt remains t10. Numerical comparisons cannot establish musical phrasing or listener preference; any actual audition observations must be documented separately.

audio_review.completion_means: Audio-input processing completed; critic validity did not pass.
audio_review.method: Every complete WAV is encoded as ordered, bar-aligned <=30s clips in one multimodal request per piece. Official HF Whisper frontend replaces the numerically different MLX native frontend. Labels, MIDI metrics, chords and selection results are withheld from the model.

calibration.silence_raw_response: The audio clip contains a segment of a pop catchy riff with a disturbing background humming. The main instrument is a bass, and there is no speech or singing. The rhythmic texture is upbeat and catchy, with a disturbing undertone created by the humming. There are no specific changes in the audio; it remains relatively consistent throughout.
calibration.result: failed: the model describes music for a zero waveform
calibration.consequence: No subjective preference, musical cadence, chord correctness or human-listening claim is supported.

audio_review.report_summary: All nine complete WAVs (15 min 25 s, including release tails) reached Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct-4bit: 39 ordered clips, each at most 30 s, with all clip embeddings in one request per piece. Every frontend input length and waveform hash was checked. Labels, MIDI statistics and preferred versions were withheld. However, an identical-prompt silence control produced invented music. This completes audio-input coverage, not a validated listening evaluation.

report_rows.observation: t08 and t10 give incompatible major/minor descriptions of the shared prompt. t10 and t12 omit clip 5 in their prose despite encoding it. Reject these unverified claims; use the preceding bar table.

All three receive generic smooth/fade descriptions despite different density trajectories. These words establish neither a preferred version nor a resolved cadence; the per-bar MIDI comparison remains the evidence.

The critic gives generic register/development descriptions rather than a checkable account of the t12 late density collapse and +16.19-semitone mean-pitch shift. Its text adds no validated quality judgment.

audio_review.report_limitations: No human listening or listener ratings were performed. The silence hallucination and omitted clip descriptions make this critic unreliable for preference or harmony claims. A synthesized release tail is not evidence of a composed cadence. Keep raw responses for audit; use MIDI for measured bar facts and listening.html for direct comparison.

rows.interpretation: The complete WAV was encoded, but the failed silence control prevents treating the model prose as a validated listening judgment. Bar facts are MIDI measurements, not human impressions.
